description: Probe-only evidence for Matmul on a padded leading stride, crossed with the declared alignment. One fixed float batched matmul (A [3,16,32] x B [3,32,128] = C [3,16,128], row-major, quick Matmul/Default template) whose leading dimension (the row stride, in elements) is the packed one plus `pad` for the tensors `pad_on` names (a, b, c, or all three); the batch stride grows with it, so each batch holds whole rows and the `pad` elements at the end of a row are gap elements that belong to no element. `pad` takes 0 (packed), the odd values 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 31, 2, 4 and 12 (4 and 12 are 16-byte multiples of a float, 2 is not), 8 and 16 (32 and 64-byte multiples) and 17, so a leading dimension is a 16-byte multiple only at 0, 4, 8, 12 and 16. It is crossed with the declared alignment of A, B and C (tensor_patches on uids 1, 2, 0, one value for all three) and with the placement of the device pointers, as in Matmul/Align and SdpaFwd/Flash2: exact puts every device pointer at exactly the declared alignment, under misaligns A (placement_uid 1) below it (a PASS then means the backend rejected the pointer), default leaves the pointers where they are; under drawn at alignment 1 is rendered as exact. It exists to show whether MIOpen and hipBLASLt compute the right matrix, or decline, when the leading dimension is not a multiple of the vector width the declared alignment promises. Expected (probed on gfx950): hipBLASLt is PASS at every pad when the declared alignment is 16, whatever the leading dimension, and DECLINED at every other alignment, as in Matmul/Align; MIOpen is DECLINED everywhere, as in Matmul/Align. WRONG, an engine that accepts a padded leading dimension and computes a different matrix, is the finding the space exists to find. pad_on has no effect at pad 0, so every pad_on but 'all' is illegal there.

derive.eff_placement: 'exact' if placement == 'under' and alignment < 2 else placement

constraints.reason: pad_on names no tensor when pad is 0: every pad_on would render the same packed graph
